title: Add cmd=version route and assertDeployedVersion_ to RCV deploy (clears gas-deploy Stage 1b blocked AC)
description:
Scoped mini-stage from GAS-Core/best-practices/gas-deployment/RECOMMENDATION.md.

Stage 1b's last AC ("Both projects deploy to SIT under pnpm with assertDeployedVersion_ passing") is blocked on RCV alone: F3Go30's half was verified live in Stage 1c, RCV has no cmd=version route and no assertDeployedVersion_.

Work (port Stage 1c's F3Go30 implementation to RCV):
1. script/WebApp.js: cmd=version route returning {ok, version, versionDate, target, deploymentId} per RECOMMENDATION.md 3.2. No secret required; must work on ANYONE_ANONYMOUS.
2. tools/manage-deployments.js: assertDeployedVersion_() polling /exec until version AND target match what was stamped; last step before printDeploySummary_; mismatch fails the deploy. Reuse tools/callWebapp.js as the HTTP client - no second client.
3. queryLiveVersion_ for --summary (never throws, returns null on failure).
4. Feed server-confirmed version into printDeploySummary_.
5. Unit tests: match / version-mismatch / target-mismatch / timeout / edge-propagation-delay, injected fake client.
6. Verify with a real pnpm run deploy:sit. SIT only, never PROD.
7. Check Stage 1b's box in RECOMMENDATION.md.

AC frozen in RECOMMENDATION.md Stage 1b + 3.2.
close_reason: cmd=version route + assertDeployedVersion_ landed in RCV; verified live against SIT (v0.1.6.2, deployment AKfycbwRGVyw…, @34→@35, 'SIT verified — serving v0.1.6.2 (target SIT)'). Version-mismatch and target-mismatch both confirmed live against the real deployment. 9 deterministic suites green. Clears gas-deploy Stage 1b's last AC; Stage 1 now fully closed. queryLiveVersion_/--summary and callWebapp --cmd deliberately left to Stage 2 - see RECOMMENDATION.md Stage 1b addendum.

title: Add unit test suite for voting algorithms (processRCV.js, processCondorcet.js)
description:
npm test currently runs test_gas_logger, test_ballot_model, test_manage_deployments, test_callwebapp — zero coverage of the five voting algorithms. That is how the blank-rank bug (RankChoiceVoting-35e) shipped.

Create test/test_voting_algorithms.js following the existing test style (plain node asserts, loaded via eval or module pattern like the other tests; processRCV.js/processCondorcet.js are bare GAS-style globals — load with fs.readFileSync + eval and stub global.Logger, as no module.exports exists; alternatively add a module.exports guard like webAdmin.js line 484 has, which is the cleaner route). Wire it into the package.json test script.

Boundary conditions to cover for RCV (runRankedChoiceVoting):
- majority winner in round 1
- winner after elimination cascade (verify redistribution)
- exhausted ballots: majority threshold must use active-ballot weights, not all ballots
- weighted ballots in first-choice counting AND in tie-breaks (RankChoiceVoting-c6n)
- partial ballots / blank ranks, incl. a candidate ranked by nobody (RankChoiceVoting-35e)
- non-contiguous ranks compressed correctly (e.g. 1,3,7 -> 1,2,3)
- tie broken by fewest second-choice; tie broken by most last-place; unresolvable tie returns {winner:null, tie:[...]}
- 2-candidate dead 50/50 tie
- single ballot; all-blank ballot; duplicate rank values on one ballot
- summary table statuses consistent with returned winner

For Condorcet family (buildPairwiseMatrix, findCondorcetWinner, findSchulzeWinner, findRankedPairsWinner, findMinimaxWinner):
- pairwise matrix correctness incl. weights and partial ballots (ranked beats unranked)
- clear Condorcet winner found by all four methods
- perfect 3-cycle: basic=null, minimax/schulze/rankedPairs behavior per their specs (rankedPairs per RankChoiceVoting-vi6)
- pairwise exact tie between two candidates
- 2 candidates only; known textbook example where Schulze winner differs from plurality
- minimax tied worst-defeat returns winner:null

Write tests to assert CORRECT behavior; tests for the three open bugs will fail until those are fixed — that is intended (fix beads are dependencies).
acceptance_criteria: test/test_voting_algorithms.js exists, wired into npm test, all listed boundary conditions asserted, npm test passes once dependency bugs are fixed.

title: Blank ranks treated as best rank: an unranked candidate can win every algorithm
description:
isNaN('') === false in JS, and '' coerces to 0 in comparisons/sorts, so every place the algorithms filter ranks with !isNaN(rank) (processRCV.js: countVotes, getEffectiveBallots, countTieWinners.countByRank) or isNaN(rankI)/(!isNaN(rankJ) && rankI < rankJ) (processCondorcet.js: buildPairwiseMatrix) treats a blank rank cell as rank 0 — i.e. BETTER than rank 1.

Verified repro (node): 3 ballots ranks [1,2,''] over candidates [A,B,C] (unanimous A>B, nobody ranks C). Result: C wins RCV with all 3 votes, and C is the Condorcet, Schulze, Ranked Pairs, and Minimax winner. Pairwise matrix comes back [[0,3,0],[0,0,0],[3,3,0]] — the unranked candidate 'beats' everyone.

Blank rank cells are real production data, not hypothetical: BallotModel.js submitBallotResponse_ (line ~783) writes '' for any candidate not in the submitted order, and response rows written before a candidate was added have blank cells under the new column (see findRespondentsWithNewCandidates_ comment, BallotModel.js ~580).

Fix: define one shared helper e.g. _isRankedValue(rank) that returns true only for finite numbers > 0 (handle numbers from getValues and possibly numeric strings; '' / null / undefined are unranked), and use it in all four sites in place of the isNaN checks. In processRCV.js the compression step already treats '' as unranked, so after compression ranks are integers or '' — the counting loops must skip ''. In buildPairwiseMatrix, semantics must be: ranked beats unranked (voter expressed preference for I but not J => I preferred over J), unranked vs unranked = no preference.
acceptance_criteria: Repro above yields A as winner for RCV and all Condorcet methods; ranked-beats-unranked counted in pairwise matrix; unranked-vs-unranked adds nothing; regression tests added covering partial ballots and a never-ranked candidate; npm test passes.

title: Cache ballot config/candidates in Script Properties to speed up static-pages loads
description: The static-pages front end (admin edit/list, ballot page) felt slow because every RPC opened the bound spreadsheet and re-read the ballot's config/Candidates sheet ranges on every load. Added BallotCache.js (script-properties cache keyed per ballot id, storing config + Candidates table), wired it into getBallotForRespondent_ (name-less loads skip the sheet entirely), getAdminEditData, and getAdminListData_. Kept fresh via: (1) every write RPC that touches config/candidates (adminSave*, adminAddCandidate, adminSaveCandidate, addBallotTopic) refreshes the cache right after writing; (2) a new onEdit(e) simple trigger (Triggers.js) rebuilds the cache when someone hand-edits a Ballot-<id> sheet directly in Sheets; (3) a cache miss transparently falls back to reading/re-populating from the sheet.
design: Response rows (who voted) are intentionally NOT cached since they change on every submission. Cache value is JSON in a single Script Property per ballot (ballotCache:<id>); refreshBallotCache_ catches quota/serialization failures and leaves the ballot uncached rather than throwing, so the sheet-read fallback always keeps things correct.
acceptance_criteria: npm test passes (new test/test_ballot_cache.js covers cache-hit/miss, all write-path refreshes, and the onEdit trigger); getBallotForRespondent_ with no name serves entirely from cache without touching SpreadsheetApp once warm.
close_reason: Implemented: BallotCache.js + Triggers.js + wiring in BallotModel.js/webAdmin.js; npm test green (new test/test_ballot_cache.js).

description: Ported the HtmlService-rendered admin/ballot pages (webAdminEditPage.html, webBallotPage.html, and the server-rendered list/analysis HTML in webAdmin.js) to a single static client (static-pages/src/index.html) calling GAS purely as a JSON API, mirroring F3Go30's static-pages strategy. doGet now redirects cmd=admin/cmd=ballot to the static front end instead of rendering HTML; doPost ?cmd=api (script/ApiBridge.js) is the new generic JSON-RPC bridge (text/plain POST body to dodge CORS preflight, same trick F3Go30 uses). Build/publish pipeline added: tools/build-static-pages.js + tools/publish-static-pages.js, wired into tools/manage-deployments.js's deploy() for all three targets. SIT/PROD publish to ../F3Static/ballot/{sit,prod} (f3go30/static-pages, namespaced alongside F3Go30's own dist/); NUUC publishes to ../Static/pub/ballot (nuuc-it/Static, single folder). New local.settings.json keys: staticPagesRepoPath, nuucStaticPagesRepoPath. Old render functions (_renderAdminList_, _renderAdminEditPage_, _renderAdminAnalysis_, generateCondorcetResultsHtml, etc.) intentionally left in place as unreachable legacy code, not deleted, to minimize risk.

Wired into npm run test:live-sit. This covers the same API surface a real browser session would exercise; a literal manual click-through in a browser is still worth doing before promoting to PROD but is no longer blocking.

title: Report true second place: current ranked lists are heuristics; compute finish order by iterative winner removal
description:
Question answered by analysis: if the first-place winner is removed, the second-place winner is NOT reliably derivable from any of the current reports — a re-run is required for every method.

Evidence (verified in node):
- RCV: center-squeeze example (8x A>B>C, 5x B>C>A, 7x C>B>A): C wins; final summary shows A as the top remaining candidate (8 votes), but re-running without C gives B (12 vs 8) as true second place. The final-round runner-up is not the second-place finisher.
- Basic Condorcet: rankedCandidates is a Copeland-style head-to-head win count; #2 by that score is not necessarily the Condorcet winner among the remaining candidates.
- Schulze: reported score (sum of path strengths) is a display heuristic; official Schulze ranking compares p[i][j] vs p[j][i]. #2 by the sum can misorder.
- Ranked Pairs: score = outgoing minus incoming locked edges is a heuristic; the real ranking is the locked graph's topological order.
- Minimax: each candidate's worst defeat includes defeats BY the winner; removing the winner changes scores, so #2 by current score is not guaranteed.

Implement: after finding each method's winner, remove that candidate and recompute to get 2nd place (optionally iterate for full finish order, stopping at ties). Cheap for the Condorcet family — buildPairwiseMatrix result can be reused by masking the winner's row/column (or just re-invoke the finders on filtered candidateNames/ranks; ballots need ranks entry removed for the winner's index). RCV needs a full re-run of runRankedChoiceVoting with the winner's candidate removed from candidateNames and each ballot's ranks (compression already handles the resulting gaps).

Reporting: add a 'Finish order' (1st, 2nd, ...) per method to _buildResultsRows_ (webAdmin.js) and the HTML in generateCondorcetResultsHtml/_renderAdminAnalysis_, and relabel the existing rankedCandidates tables to make clear the score is a heuristic display, not the finish order. Keep runtime bounded: n candidates => at most n-1 re-runs; fine at this scale.

Depends on the blank-rank fix (RankChoiceVoting-35e) since removing a winner from ballots must not reintroduce rank-gap bugs.
acceptance_criteria: Center-squeeze example reports B as RCV 2nd place; each Condorcet method reports 2nd place computed with winner removed; ties during iteration are reported, not silently ordered; covered by tests.

title: Ranked Pairs silently picks an order-dependent winner on cycles and pairwise ties
description:
processCondorcet.js findRankedPairsWinner: (1) pairs with equal margin are locked in candidate-enumeration order (Array.sort is stable, pairs pushed in i,j index order), and (2) the winner is the FIRST source found by index — if the locked graph has multiple sources it silently returns the lowest-indexed one.

Verified repros (node):
- Perfect 3-cycle (A>B>C, B>C>A, C>A>B, one ballot each): Condorcet, Schulze, and Minimax all correctly return winner=null; Ranked Pairs returns 'A' purely because the A→B edge was enumerated first. Reordering the candidate list changes the winner.
- Dead pairwise tie (A>B>C and B>A>C, one ballot each): locked graph has two sources (A and B); function reports winner 'A' with no indication B is exactly tied.

Fix: after locking, collect ALL sources. If exactly one, return it as winner. If more than one, return winner:null plus a tie field listing the tied sources (mirror the {winner, tie} shape used by runRankedChoiceVoting so callers can render it). Also detect the equal-margin ambiguity case if feasible, or at minimum document in the JSDoc that equal-margin pairs are locked in enumeration order. Update onOpen.js generateCondorcetResultsHtml and webAdmin.js _buildResultsRows_ to render the tie list instead of just 'None (cycle)'.
acceptance_criteria: Perfect-cycle repro no longer returns a winner from Ranked Pairs; multi-source repro reports both tied candidates; rendering shows the tie; regression tests added; npm test passes.
notes: Implementation complete: findRankedPairsWinner in script/processCondorcet.js now detects multi-source and equal-margin-ambiguity cases and returns {winner:null, tie:[...]}; onOpen.js and webAdmin.js render the tie list; 3 regression tests added to test/test_voting_algorithms.js; npm test passes. Not committed/closed per unattended-session protocol - runner will commit/close.

title: RCV tie-break ignores ballot weights (counts ballots, not votes)
description:
processRCV.js countTieWinners.countByRank increments counts[name]++ per ballot instead of adding ballot.weight, while the main countVotes and _sumBallotWeights honor weights. So the second-choice and last-place tie-breakers count ballots, not weighted votes.

Verified repro (node): candidates [A,B,C]; ballots (ranks[i] = rank of candidate i): {[3,2,1] w3}, {[2,3,1] w1}, {[2,3,1] w1}, {[1,2,3] w3}, {[2,1,3] w3}. First-place: C=5, A=3, B=3 (total 11, no majority); A/B tie for elimination. Second-choice votes: B=3 (one weight-3 ballot), A=2 (two weight-1 ballots) — A should be eliminated for fewest second-choice votes. Actual: B eliminated with reason 'fewest second choice votes' because ballot counts are A=2, B=1.

Fix: in countByRank, add (ballot.weight || 1) instead of ++.

Same file, related decision to confirm while in there: countByRank counts rank positions over ALL candidates on the ballot including already-eliminated ones (e.g. 'second choice' can be an eliminated candidate). Document the chosen semantics in the JSDoc either way.
acceptance_criteria: Repro above eliminates A (not B) with reason 'fewest second choice votes'; regression test added; npm test passes.
notes: Fix applied and verified: countByRank in script/processRCV.js weights votes by ballot.weight; regression test added; npm test passes. Ready for review/close by runner.

title: Add Link Text/Link URL columns to Candidates sheet
description: Voters should be able to see an optional hyperlink (opening in a new tab) in a candidate's expanded detail view, and admins need to edit it. Adds Link Text/Link URL columns to the [Candidates] section, threads them through BallotModel read/write + RPCs, renders the link in webBallotPage.html's detail toggle, and adds edit/add fields in webAdminEditPage.html.

title: Rename Survey terminology to Ballot across code and docs
description: Rename the poll/entity concept from 'Survey' to 'Ballot' throughout the codebase and docs (Survey-<id> sheet -> Ballot-<id>, SurveyModel.js -> BallotModel.js, webSurvey.js/webSurveyPage.html -> webBallot.js/webBallotPage.html, cmd=survey -> cmd=ballot, admin UI text, README, work-log.md). Leave script/processRCV.js's existing 'ballot' usage (a single voter's ranked submission) untouched -- that is a distinct, standard election-science sense of the word and does not collide since it never used 'survey'.

title: Audit Drive fallback usage and remove obsolete Google Forms workflows
description: Copilot flagged that GasLogger.js's Drive fallback (DriveApp.getFolderById at line ~150, DriveApp.getFileById at line ~237) needs oauthScopes that aren't currently declared in script/appsscript.json. Before just adding the scope, verify whether this Drive fallback path is still a real use case for this project: PR #1 migrated RankChoiceVoting from a Google Forms-based workflow to a self-contained webapp deployment (SurveyModel.js/WebApp.js/webSurvey.js), and the Forms-era code paths may no longer need Drive access at all. Separately, any remaining Google Forms-related workflows/scripts in this repo are stale now that the webapp approach has replaced Forms as the survey front-end and should be removed.
acceptance_criteria: Done when: (1) each call site using getFolderById/getFileById is traced to confirm whether it is still reachable from the current webapp-only flow; (2) if still needed, appsscript.json's oauthScopes is updated to include the required Drive scope; if not needed, the dead code is removed instead; (3) any Google Forms-specific workflow code/docs still present in the repo are identified and removed, since the webapp deployment replaced Forms as the survey delivery mechanism.
close_reason: Deleted Forms-era files (createRCVform.js, cleanResponses.js, testRCV.js) and Forms-only wrapper functions (processRankedChoiceVotes, processCondorcetVoting); removed corresponding onOpen.js menu items. Confirmed GasLogger.js Drive usage and appsscript.json oauthScopes are unrelated (active webapp features), no changes needed there.

title: RCV reporting/doc cleanups: summary Winner threshold, tie-break docs contradict code, misc
description:
Small correctness/clarity items in processRCV.js found during algorithm review:

1. getCandidateSummaryTable labels a candidate 'Winner' when votes > _sumBallotWeights(allBallots)/2 (ALL ballots), but the actual winner check in the main loop uses only active (non-exhausted) ballots. With exhausted ballots the summary can show the actual winner as 'Active'. Make the summary use the same active-ballot threshold (reachable once RankChoiceVoting-35e lands and partial ballots count correctly). Also hoist the _sumBallotWeights call out of the per-candidate loop.

2. Docs contradict the implementation on tie-break #2: file header (line 5) says 'least last-place votes' and breakTie JSDoc says 'eliminates the candidate with the fewest last-place votes', but countTieWinners mode 'mostLastPlace' uses Math.max and the elimination reason string is 'most last-place votes'. The implementation (eliminate the candidate MOST often ranked last) is the sensible direction — fix the two doc comments to match the code.

3. getCandidateSummaryTable sort comment says 'eliminated by round asc' but the comparator returns b.round - a.round (desc). Desc (last-eliminated first) is the more useful order; fix the comment.

4. logProgress(roundNumber, eliminate, getEffectiveBallots()) at line ~269 passes a third arg logProgress doesn't accept — drop it (avoids the wasted getEffectiveBallots computation).

5. findMinimaxWinner returns winner:null on tied minimax scores and reporting labels it 'None (tie/cycle)' — but callers' HTML ('cycle detected') is misleading for a plain tie. Also its 'worst defeat' uses max of d[j][i] even when i beats j (pairwise-opposition variant) — document the variant in the JSDoc.
acceptance_criteria: Summary status matches returned winner in exhausted-ballot scenarios; doc comments match implementation; no behavior change beyond item 1; npm test passes.
